unit.title: Relative clauses
unit.subtitle: que, quien, lo que, donde and cuyo: joining ideas smoothly

grammar.title: Linking two ideas into one sentence
grammar.intro: Relative clauses let you add information without starting a new sentence — “the book that I read,” “the person with whom I speak.” The workhorse is que. Add quien after prepositions, lo que for “what,” donde for places, and cuyo for “whose.” Master these five and your Spanish flows.

sections.heading: que — the all-purpose relative
sections.body: que covers “that / which / who” for things and people alike. It's by far the most common:

ex.en: The book that I read is interesting.

ex.es: La chica que canta es mi prima.
ex.en: The girl who sings is my cousin.

sections.heading: quien after prepositions · lo que for “what”
sections.body: After a preposition (con, de, para…), use quien/quienes for people. Use lo que for “what / that which” (an idea, not a named noun):

ex.es: La persona con quien hablo es médica.
ex.en: The person with whom I speak is a doctor.

sections.heading: donde for places · cuyo for “whose”
sections.body: Use donde for places. Use cuyo for “whose” — and remember it agrees with the thing owned, not the owner (cuyo/cuya/cuyos/cuyas):

ex.en: The house where I live is small.
The house whose roof is red.

takeaways: que = that/which/who — the default for people and things.
After a preposition, use quien/quienes for people: con quien.
cuyo (whose) agrees with the thing owned: cuyo tejado, cuya puerta.

mistakes.w: La persona que hablo con es médica.
mistakes.r: La persona con quien hablo es médica.
mistakes.why: Don't strand the preposition; put it before quien: con quien hablo.

mistakes.w: La casa cuya tejado es rojo.
mistakes.r: La casa cuyo tejado es rojo.
mistakes.why: Cuyo agrees with the thing owned (tejado, masculine), not the owner.
For “what / that which” you need lo que, not bare que.

exercises.prompt: El libro ___ leí es muy bueno.
exercises.prompt_en: The book that I read is very good.
exercises.no: The default relative for a thing is “que”: el libro que leí.

exercises.prompt: La persona con ___ hablo es médica.
exercises.prompt_en: The person with whom I speak is a doctor.
exercises.ok: ¡Exacto! Tras preposición y persona → con quien.
exercises.no: After a preposition, use quien for people: “con quien hablo”.
“Lo que dices es verdad” — use lo que for “what / that which”.

exercises.prompt: La casa ___ tejado es rojo es antigua.
exercises.prompt_en: The house whose roof is red is old.
exercises.no: Cuyo agrees with the thing owned (tejado, masc.): “cuyo tejado”.

exercises.prompt: Match each relative word to its meaning.

exercises.tts: La casa donde vivo es pequeña.
accepted: la casa donde vivo es pequena
la casa donde vivo es pequeña
exercises.translation: The house where I live is small.
exercises.no: It was: “La casa donde vivo es pequeña.” (The house where I live is small.)

exercises.scenario: Pointing out a friend at a party 🎉

options.text: Es la amiga con quien estudio español.
Es la amiga que estudio español con.
Es la amiga lo que estudio español.

exercises.no: Put the preposition before quien: “la amiga con quien estudio español”.

exercises.say: La persona con quien hablo es médica
exercises.en: The person with whom I speak is a doctor
exercises.no: Almost — tap “Hear it”, then match the rhythm of “con quien hablo”.
